document.title: Eyewitness to the Fall of Herat Says Taliban are Winning Hearts and Minds - For Now
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Confidential] An American citizen who witnessed the fall of Herat faults Ismail Khan's political and military ineptitude. He says the Taliban were extremely well organized, well-financed and strongly disciplined.

events.description: Ismael Khan's forces pushed the Taliban back from Delarum to Girishk, then were cut off and routed at Girishk after a NIFA commander was bribed.
Shindand air base fell to the Taliban before Ismael Khan could organize its defense.
Fall of Herat to the Taliban; Ismael Khan fled to Iran with about 1,000 troops after emptying the bank.
Taliban occupied facilities, set a curfew, freed prisoners, doubled salaries and moved captured weapons to Kandahar.
Mohammed Omar addressed Heratis after Friday prayers at the main mosque.
U.S. Embassy political officer met an American eyewitness who returned from Herat on 16 Sept.
Taliban seized Herat and moved captured weapons from Ismael Khan's forces to Kandahar within three days.
Iran re-opened border posts closed at the Taliban takeover of Herat; Torghundi crossing open.
Mohammed Omar addressed Heratis after Friday prayers at the main mosque but failed to impress them.
Taliban closed girls' schools and told women not to work; senior Herati ulema protested.
U.S. Embassy Islamabad sent cable on eyewitness account of the fall of Herat.
AmCit source returned from Herat on a UN flight after witnessing the Taliban takeover.
US Embassy political officer met the eyewitness to Herat's fall.
Taliban defeated Ismael Khan's forces at Girishk after a NIFA commander was bribed; hundreds killed or captured.
Ismael Khan's forces pushed Taliban back from Delarum to Girishk.
Shindand air base fell before Ismael Khan could organize defense.
On the night Herat fell, Ismael Khan emptied the bank and fled to Iran with 1,000 troops.
Taliban occupied Herat, set checkpoints, curfew, released prisoners, doubled salaries, moved weapons to Kandahar.
Repeated aerial bombing of Herat airport and other military targets.

sources_cited: Interview with an unnamed American eyewitness (AMCIT) who returned from Herat on a UN flight, 17 Sept 1995
key_claims: Herat fell mainly because Ismael Khan lost the support of his commanders, not because of Taliban fighting prowess.
The Taliban were well organized, well financed and disciplined, paying for goods and doubling public servants' salaries.
The Taliban closed girls' schools and barred women from work, causing friction with liberal Herat and Dari-speaking residents.
Heratis increasingly suspected that Taliban organization and money came from outside, and Pakistani control would undermine support.
Many Heratis believed the Taliban were backed by the US and UN and would restore Zahir Shah.
